atomic_claims.claim_text: Dispersion-based seurat and cell_ranger HVG flavors require logarithmized expression.
seurat_v3 and seurat_v3_paper HVG flavors require count data.
The operator records a boolean highly-variable feature indicator.
Scanpy PCA accepts cell-by-gene expression from the selected matrix or layer without a universal HVG requirement.
PCA may use a feature mask; if no mask is specified, Scanpy uses highly_variable when available and otherwise all features.
The scKG Scanpy Core project profile chooses scaled HVG expression for its controlled PCA step; this is not a universal Scanpy requirement.
Scanpy neighbors accepts X or a named obsm representation; PCA is an automatic/default path rather than a universal prerequisite.
atomic_claims.object_value: X or any compatible obsm embedding

atomic_claims.claim_text: Scanpy neighbors stores distances, connectivities and metadata that names their keys and construction parameters.
Scanpy UMAP resolves neighbor settings and connectivities through neighbors_key.
Scanpy Leiden consumes an explicit sparse adjacency or the connectivities selected from a neighbor graph; UMAP is not an input.
Scanpy Leiden records categorical cluster labels and clustering parameters.
The generic Harmony interface accepts a cell embedding matrix with aligned metadata and categorical covariates.
The Seurat Harmony interface defaults to a precomputed PCA reduction, while the generic interface is not restricted to PCA.
Harmony requires cell-aligned metadata and names the categorical covariates to integrate.
Harmony returns a corrected embedding matrix, not corrected expression counts.
Scrublet requires a cell-by-gene raw unnormalized UMI count matrix.
Scrublet returns continuous doublet scores and threshold-derived predicted doublet calls.
Multiple samples or capture units should be analyzed separately because merged proportions may violate Scrublet's assumptions.
The automatically selected Scrublet threshold should be diagnosed and adjusted when necessary.
Scores and predicted calls are evidence for review; they do not themselves authorize automatic cell deletion.
SingleR accepts a gene-by-cell query matrix, including raw UMI counts or transcript counts without normalization and log transformation.
atomic_claims.object_value: raw counts or log expression query matrix

atomic_claims.claim_text: SingleR requires reference expression, usually normalized and log-transformed for automatic marker detection.
SingleR requires a known label for each reference sample.
SingleR restricts analysis to the reference-query gene intersection and rejects an empty intersection.
Reference applicability must be reviewed because absent target labels can yield uncertain or incorrect assignments.

description: Corrected candidate-only decision rules for Scanpy Core, Harmony, Scrublet and SingleR.

entities.label: scKG project profile PCA on scaled HVGs

cross_port_alignment_constraints: expression and optional feature mask must share ordered feature identity
embedding rows and covariate rows must identify the same cells in the same order
covariate rows must align to embedding cells
query and reference must have a non-empty feature intersection in a compatible feature namespace
reference expression columns and label entries must have identical ordered reference ids
one known label is required for every reference sample

entities.label: Scrublet should be run separately per capture/sample unit
doublet scores/calls do not authorize automatic cell deletion
reference label space may not cover the query biology
